segment:
Mara wanted to ask him, so she did. “Do you mind if I sit?”
“Oh. Sure.” Jonah let go of her hand and backed up toward the couch.

Mara watched him sit down as she walked over to take the chair on the opposite side. The room was simple enough, but not dull. She liked the way the light fell on the smooth fabric of the wall padding and the sleek lines of the white furniture, the way the table had only a few thin legs that bent slightly outward from a square of metal and glass.
She’d felt at home as soon as she entered Fulcrum. And it didn’t feel like an illusion; she wasn’t just trying to prove anything here. It seemed real, and for once that didn’t scare her away.
She sat down, leaned back, and crossed one leg over the other, looking at this Jonah through him at all of them, curious how he would respond.
text:
When Mara walked into the common room at six fifteen, someone was already there. Someone younger, it seemed.
She couldn’t make out the face behind the blond hair. But the body was fine enough, leaning back on the couch with bare legs crossed and arms flung in opposite directions, one palm pressing the padded wall and the other wrist resting on the low table beside him.
She stood stock-still by the doorway for a moment, aware of her breath and of his awareness that she was here. He stirred and tilted his head; a face turned toward her, expressionless.

The two pairs of eyes held each other through an entire exhale.
And then the young man had pushed himself up on the armrests, stretched to his full height, and strolled over to shake her hand.
“Mara?”
He was closer than she would have guessed from where he’d been sitting, broad-shouldered and strong-chinned in a white T-shirt, grinning at her through dark-framed glasses as he reached out for the handshake. She took it.
“Jonah,” he said.
“Hello,” she replied, and then they stood there, still shaking hands, not knowing what to do next.

Mara wanted to ask him, so she did. “Do you mind if I sit?”
“Oh. Sure.” Jonah let go of her hand and backed up toward the couch.

Mara watched him sit down as she walked over to take the chair on the opposite side. The room was simple enough, but not dull. She liked the way the light fell on the smooth fabric of the wall padding and the sleek lines of the white furniture, the way the table had only a few thin legs that bent slightly outward from a square of metal and glass.
She’d felt at home as soon as she entered Fulcrum. And it didn’t feel like an illusion; she wasn’t just trying to prove anything here. It seemed real, and for once that didn’t scare her away.
She sat down, leaned back, and crossed one leg over the other, looking at this Jonah through him at all of them, curious how he would respond.

segment:
He had an unusually firm grip. It took her a moment to realize he wasn’t the sort of guy who’d insist on keeping eye contact; in fact, he’d broken it himself and was now watching his right shoe pivot on a gray-painted concrete floor. She let go.
“You look nice,” he said suddenly, straightening up from looking at his shoe. She laughed.
“Thanks. You, too.”

The blond fellow turned her way again, and this time there was no sign of the blank look she’d seen in him a few moments ago; his expression had changed to something more easygoing and welcoming. But underneath all that openness there lurked an air of mystery about him that intrigued Mara.
He led her back toward where he’d been sitting before. “Do you like tea or coffee?” he asked. “We can fix you up with something.”

segment:
Jonah cleared his throat and pulled his hand away with the air of someone having just realized the room was on fire. He shoved his hands in his pockets and glanced toward the couch. “Would you like a seat?”
“Of course,” she said, smiling, “thank you.” And they went to the couch together and sat down.
She looked over at Jonah, and he was looking at her with an expression that seemed both curious and slightly embarrassed, like a little boy who’d been told to show her his favorite toy but felt uncomfortably aware of his pants being down.

Mara put one of her hands over the other and rested them both on top of her knees. A subtle tension was holding her whole body rigid.
“I’m sorry if I’m interrupting,” she said, “I didn’t realize there would be others here this early.”

segment:
She laughed and dropped his hand.
“I’ve never seen this place,” she confessed. “Is it all right to come in and hang around?”

He looked surprised, and then he laughed too. “I’m pretty sure the entire purpose of having a common room is that you’re allowed to come in and hang around. As long as Adrian’s not in here.”

“He wouldn’t object?”

“Oh, he would,” said Jonah, laughing again. “But if you’re here for long, you’ll probably get used to that. He’s always objecting to something. Right now we’ve been banned from bringing laptops into this room.”

Mara was already thinking that she liked him; she liked the way he looked at her as they talked, and the way his grin pulled his cheeks back.

“And what did you say your name was?”
